body: P1 DESIGN CHECKPOINT before edit — the ruling’s adversarial condition exposes a carrier gap, so the literal one-line None fix is NOT sufficient. Counterexample under current aggregate: eligible external observations [Some(1), Some(0)] score 0.5; if the channel abstains only on the failure, [Some(1), None] scores 1.0 because aggregate drops None. Coverage falls, but the published accuracy doubles: exactly the forbidden renormalization. Also UnitObservation.value: Option[Double] currently uses None for INELIGIBLE units, so it cannot represent ELIGIBLE-BUT-MISSING support; Coverage.of(obs.size, observed.size) then calls every recall unit eligible, contrary to Coverage’s own meaning. RECOMMENDATION: a typed MetricObservation ADT = Ineligible | Observed(Double) | Missing(MissingReason); UnitObservation carries it. Existing metric Option paths map to Ineligible; the external rule maps an Unranked eligible row to Missing(ProviderAbstained). Aggregation counts only non-Ineligible units as eligible, and if ANY eligible unit is explicitly Missing, returns Estimate.Missing(reason) with observed/eligible Coverage and no point/CI, rather than conditioning on survivors. Then selective abstention cannot improve the score: it removes the point estimate and exposes 1/2 support. When all eligible observations are present, existing story-macro arithmetic is unchanged. This is the smallest structural fix I see that satisfies both hard-classification abstention and no-renormalization; treating missing as zero would violate abstention, while dropping it violates the regression. It introduces public typed vocabulary and changes coverage semantics, so I need chief approval per governance before hardening it. Expected paths: metrics.scala, MetricsSuite, LeakageSuite, WogDiagnosticSuite; MetricsSuite overlaps m1’s pending route-support amendment, so please sequence m1-first or this P1-first. Bead claimed/doing; no reservation or edit yet.
